subject: Clarify assessment surface for Acme Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Jamie Collins <jamie.collins@acmepay.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: security-assessments@acmepay.com
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Assessment scope for Dedicated deployment (Acme)

Hi Aisha,

We're lining up an external penetration test for our integration with Redwood and need to confirm what parts of the stack Redwood considers in-scope for the assessment. Our vendor will perform both internet-facing and tenant-level tests (they sometimes simulate an authenticated tenant). Can you confirm the following for our Dedicated deployment: 

- Are the Dedicated GPU nodes (in the customer-dedicated pool) considered Redwood-managed and therefore in-scope?
- Are control plane endpoints (management APIs, fleet orchestration) included?
- Does the scope include any host-level testing on the GPU instances or is that disallowed without special arrangements?
- For Private/VPC deployments, do you allow tenant-simulated tests (from inside VPC) or is that excluded?

We will need the penetration test report (redacted if necessary), a list of IP addresses your external testing will originate from (so we can allow them in our firewall), asset inventory, and a short mapping of which systems are Redwood-owned vs customer-owned. Attached is our assessment intake form.

Timing: we are targeting the week of June 21 for the vendor engagement. Please let us know any exclusions or additional approvals we must provide.

Thanks,
Jamie Collins
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments

Attachment: Acme_Assessment_Form.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 84 KB)

From: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
To: Jamie Collins <jamie.collins@acmepay.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, elliot.price@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Assessment scope for Dedicated deployment (Acme)

Hi Jamie — thanks for the intake form and heads up on timing. Below is a concise mapping we can share publicly and a note on practical constraints. I copied Kim (security) and Elliot (platform ops) to confirm details and provide any required artifacts.

High-level scope matrix (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed):

- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted, public): IN SCOPE — includes public inference gateways, API ingress, control-plane API endpoints used by customers.
- Dedicated (customer-reserved GPU pool): PARTIALLY IN SCOPE — Redwood manages the serving runtime (inference process, runtime OS image we ship) and network ingress for the Dedicated pool. However, tenant data stores that customers attach (customer-managed Redis/S3 endpoints) are OUT OF SCOPE unless you ask us to include them.
- Private / VPC connectors: IN SCOPE (networking boundary limited) — We consider the Redwood-managed connectors and the egress/ingress proxies in scope. Customer-managed resources inside their VPC (private databases, internal services) are OUT OF-SCOPE unless explicitly agreed.
- On-prem / air-gapped private installs: OUT OF SCOPE by default — any on-prem installations that are fully customer-hosted are governed by the customer's rules and we do not permit external testing against those hosts without a formal customer-run engagement and signed waiver.

Notes / constraints:
- Host-level (kernel, hypervisor) active exploitation tests on Dedicated instances require pre-approval and an agreed test window. We typically restrict destructive tests and require agent-based snapshots or read-only evidence collection instead.
- We can provide a redacted pen-test report for Redwood infrastructure and a separate appendix describing customer-owned connectors.
- We will also provide a short asset inventory CSV and the public IPs the Redwood external tests would use.

Artifacts we can provide now:
- redwood_scope_matrix.csv (mapping of component -> owner -> in-scope/out-of-scope)
- redwood_pen_test_brief.pdf (our standard penetration testing policy and constraints)
- network diagram + sample firewall rules (on request)

Proposed next step: 30-minute call early next week to align on the exact test cases and finalize allowed IP ranges. If that works, please propose a few times.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
+aisha@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_scope_matrix.csv (text/csv, 6 KB)

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com, Jamie Collins <jamie.collins@acmepay.com>
Cc: elliot.price@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Assessment scope for Dedicated deployment (Acme)

On Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:30:00 -0700, aisha.rahman@redwood.com wrote:
> High-level scope matrix (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed):
> 
> - Hosted API (Redwood-hosted, public): IN SCOPE ...

Thanks Aisha — adding a few security-side guardrails to set expectations for Acme and the assessor: 

1) Proof-of-consent: For any tenant-authenticated testing (simulating an Acme user inside a tenant), we need a signed vendor authorization form from Acme — the assessor must be explicitly authorized by your security team because tests touch customer data paths.

2) Host-level tests: active exploitation that could impair service (kernel/hypervisor) is prohibited on Dedicated nodes unless we run the test in an isolated canary sandbox we create. If Acme wants host-level coverage, we can arrange a scheduled sandbox window; that requires at least two weeks notice and a brief test plan.

3) Remediation evidence: We can provide remediation tickets and timelines from our issue tracker for any findings that affect Redwood-managed surfaces. See SEC ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1243. We will redact customer-identifying details in the public report.

4) IP allowlist: We will share the external testing IPs for Redwood-originated validation and can provide a CIDR list to Acme to allow in their perimeter.

Elliot — can your team confirm the IP ranges and provide a non-production canary sandbox option (if they want host-level)?

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Security — Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Collins <jamie.collins@acmepay.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.com
Cc: security-assessments@acmepay.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Assessment scope for Dedicated deployment (Acme)

Thanks Aisha and Kim — this is very helpful. Confirming next steps from our side: 

- We'll sign and return the vendor authorization form for tenant-level tests.
- We do not require host-level destructive tests initially; we'll start with application-level and tenant-simulated scenarios. If we need a host sandbox later, we'll request the canary window with the two-week lead time.
- Please send the redacted past pen-test report and the asset mapping CSV when convenient. We also need the IP ranges you mentioned so our edge team can pre-authorize the assessor.

Proposed call: Tue Jun 22 at 10:00 PT — is that open for your team?

Attached is a filled copy of our intake form.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,
Jamie Collins
Security Program Manager
Acme Payments
